title: Answer ARP only from the interface that owns the address
head: 994961c2a180
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The aarch64 settings package replaces the changed sysctl drop-in with an older one-line network configuration
leads.consequence: On aarch64, the packaging here-doc overwrites both new ARP lines before installation. A new install never boots with them; an existing install's migration loads the shortened installed file, exits successfully and records its marker while the ARP defaults remain unchanged. Update both package variants' aarch64 here-doc alongside this change, or derive that variant from the common network-only keys.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; coordinator verified omarchy-pkgs e7da505 PKGBUILD aarch64 block; published

leads.summary: A locally edited sysctl file prevents the ARP settings from reaching existing installs
leads.consequence: The settings package declares this exact /etc/sysctl.d file in backup=(). If an existing user modified it, pacman preserves it and writes the new content to .pacnew instead. sysctl -p loads the old file by exact path, returns success without the ARP lines, and omarchy-migrate marks this one-shot migration done; systemd-sysctl ignores .pacnew on every boot. No reboot or rerunning migration applies the feature until the admin merges the .pacnew. The migration should check for the keys or indicate that manual .pacnew merging is necessary, and avoid claiming success if absent.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4; generic pacman backup behaviour; not published

leads.summary: A failed sudo/sysctl -p permanently completes the migration without applying either new setting
leads.consequence: An unavailable sudo authorization, missing/unreadable installed file, or rejected sysctl key produces a nonzero exit; || true makes the script return zero and the runner touches its per-user marker. stdout is discarded; sudo/sysctl stderr may be visible in the update log, but the update continues as though successful and omarchy-migrate will skip it on later runs. For missing file or write failure, neither key takes effect until a working boot config is installed and boot runs; a reboot will not help if the file stays missing. Unlike the BBR migration, no reboot-required marker is raised. Require successful application or at least check and report actual keys before consuming the migration marker.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; coordinator verified 1789294350.sh and migrations.md; published as Migration pattern note

leads.summary: The immediate migration bypasses a later administrator sysctl.d override, including an explicit ARP-off setting
leads.consequence: If an administrator's later-named .conf deliberately sets all.arp_ignore=8 (stop replying) or sets all.arp_ignore=0 to preserve a local ARP setup, systemd-sysctl processes that later file at boot, but the migration's sysctl -p of only the Omarchy file overwrites the running all value with 1. In the 8 case it re-enables replies until the next boot/reapplication of the admin override; with 0 it suppresses replies for non-owned addresses until next boot, potentially breaking a deliberately configured virtual IP. sysctl -p also reapplies the unrelated vm and TCP settings in the same file, overriding runtime tuning. Respect existing effective config or do not promise the migration respects custom overrides.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q3 minor note; shared with earlier migrations; not published

leads.summary: Applying the keys live does not immediately correct a router's existing wrong ARP entry
leads.consequence: If the router already cached the Wi-Fi MAC for the wired IPv4, writing arp_ignore/arp_announce only changes future reply/request policy and does not invalidate the router's neighbor cache or send corrective gratuitous ARP for the wired address. The described download can continue arriving over Wi-Fi until the peer's entry expires, a new ARP request is triggered or a separate neighbor announcement is sent. This does not require a reboot in principle, but the migration's unqualified immediate-fix wording is misleading for the reproduced scenario. Qualify the claim and, if immediate repair is required, explicitly arrange a safe peer announcement/neighbor refresh.

leads.summary: Two non-stacked open PRs also edit this sysctl file, and pairwise merges have conflict markers
leads.consequence: #13311 also appends lines at the former EOF; merging either into a tree with the other creates a conflict between the ARP block and dev.tty.ldisc_autoload=0 (merges/13311-merged.conf:44-60). #9288 adds kernel.kptr_restrict and has an older base, and the pairwise merge conflicts near the initial TCP settings (merges/9288-merged.conf:4-16). Maintainers must resolve both while retaining both PRs' keys and their unrelated BBR/fq lines. GitHub's mergeable flag for each open PR describes merging into current quattro, not combining these two heads. No new test changes in this PR; #13311's and #9288's individual sysctl tests do not test a combined file.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F8 (#13311, #9288); trivial merge conflicts; not published

leads.summary: A loopback-routed or secondary address owned by another interface stops receiving ARP replies on the LAN interface
leads.consequence: For an on-link IPv4 assigned only to lo or another virtual interface, but intentionally reached via the physical Ethernet/Wi-Fi interface (for instance a virtual service address or a test/dev setup), the previous weak-host behavior let the physical interface reply to ARP for that address. With all.arp_ignore=1, inet_confirm_addr checks only the incoming physical interface and rejects that request, so new peers cannot resolve the service address. Ordinary secondary IPs assigned to the incoming physical NIC still work. This is broader than the PR's 'only LVS/DSR' risk statement; document opt-out/attach the address to the ingress NIC when such use is supported.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q1/Q2 table; covered by PR's LVS/DSR caveat; not published

leads.summary: arp_announce=2 does not guarantee ARP packets source an IPv4 owned by the outgoing interface
leads.consequence: For an unnumbered interface with a static route/neighbor to a reachable target but no local IPv4 address, Linux's arp_solicit uses inet_select_addr, which falls back across other devices. With multiple addresses on one interface it preferentially selects a primary rather than the packet's bound secondary address. The strong-host/source-own-address wording is false in those edge cases; this setting selects a preferred ARP sender where available, not a strict own-interface invariant. The common numbered Wi-Fi plus Ethernet case still gets the intended preference.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q1/Q2 table; covered by PR's LVS/DSR caveat; not published

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the two sysctl keys do what the PR describes on the Linux 7.2 kernels Omarchy ships. There are two suggestions: the keys do not reach aarch64 installs, and the migration could follow the newer BBR migration's pattern.

**Verified** from source (Linux v7.2, systemd v262, ufw 0.36.2):

| Question | Result |
|---|---|
| Does `conf.all` cover every interface? | Yes. `IN_DEV_ARP_IGNORE` and `IN_DEV_ARP_ANNOUNCE` take the larger of the `all` value and the interface's own value (`include/linux/inetdevice.h`). Interfaces added later, such as a hot-plugged USB dock adapter, are covered too, so no `conf.default` line is needed. |
| `arp_ignore=1` | An interface answers ARP only for addresses configured on itself. Wi-Fi stops answering for the Ethernet address, and the reverse. This also applies to duplicate-address probes, one likely source of the NetworkManager "conflict with own MAC" log. |
| `arp_announce=2` | ARP requests use a primary address of the outgoing interface when it has one. |
| "rp_filter is already loose (2)" | Correct in effect. systemd sets it to 2 per interface. ufw's own sysctl file sets `conf.all.rp_filter=1`, so on a default Omarchy install (ufw enabled) `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter` reads 1. The kernel uses the larger value, so the effective mode stays loose, and the asymmetric Wi-Fi-in, cable-out path is not dropped. |
| IPv6, WireGuard/Tailscale, Docker/libvirt bridges, NetworkManager hotspot | No breakage found. |

### aarch64 installs never receive the new keys

In `omacom/omarchy-pkgs`, `pkgbuilds/omarchy-settings/PKGBUILD` (and the same block in `omarchy-settings-dev`) overwrites this file when `CARCH == aarch64`:

```bash
cat >"$pkgdir/etc/sysctl.d/99-omarchy-sysctl.conf" <<'EOF'
# Solve common flakiness with SSH (MTU discovery on flaky links).
net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
EOF
```

The comment above it says "Keep only the network tuning". It was written before the BBR keys existed and does not include them.

**Impact:** on Apple Silicon installs, the ARP fix never ships, and the new migration prints "Stop wifi answering ARP for the wired interface" but reloads a file without those keys. A docked Apple Silicon laptop with Wi-Fi still connected can hit the same problem the PR describes.

**Suggested change:** add the two `net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_*` lines to the aarch64 version of the file in `omarchy-pkgs`, or note in the PR that the fix is x86_64-only.

**Migration pattern:** `migrations/1789544469.sh` copies the older zram migration (`sudo sysctl -p … || true`). The newer BBR migration `1789294350.sh`, already in the merge base, checks the live values first and asks for a reboot if the reload fails. `agents/skills/migrations.md` also asks migrations to check existing state before changing it. With the current version, every user on the machine gets a sudo call even when the values are already live, and a failed reload still marks the migration complete, without the reboot-required hint. Suggested change, following `1789294350.sh`:

```bash
echo "Stop wifi answering ARP for the wired interface"

if [[ $(sysctl -n net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_ignore) == 1 && $(sysctl -n net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_announce) == 2 ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-omarchy-sysctl.conf >/dev/null || omarchy-state set reboot-required
```

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head `994961c2`, Linux v7.2 networking source and documentation, systemd v262 and ufw 0.36.2 sysctl defaults, NetworkManager 1.58.1 route metrics, and the `omarchy-pkgs` packaging recipes. No network experiment was run, and the migration was not executed. The author's hardware measurements were not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
